newsitem.title: USA: Florida wants death penalty for rapist-mutilator.
newsitem.headline: Florida wants death penalty for rapist-mutilator.

text.p: Prosecutors investigating the murder of a prostitute vowed on Friday to seek the death penalty against Lawrence Singleton, who was free after serving eight years of a 14-year sentence for raping and mutilating a California teenager.
Singleton, 69, dressed in an orange prison jumpsuit, made a brief appearance in a Tampa court on Friday. No plea was entered and he was held without bond, the prosecutor's office said.
Prosecutors will seek the death penalty, said assistant state attorney Kim Helper.
Singleton has been charged by police with first degree murder.

He was arrested on Wednesday after police found the nude body of Roxanna Hayes, 31, lying in a pool of blood in his house. Police said Hayes had multiple stab wounds. She had 99 arrests, mostly for prostitution.

Singleton gained nationwide notoriety when he was convicted in California of raping a 15-year-old girl and then chopping off her arms in 1978. When he was released on parole, no community in California would take him and he moved to Florida.
An evaluation of Singleton while he was still in a California prison found him to be a paranoid schizophrenic with a strong potential for future violence.
Sheriff Cal Henderson acknowledged on Friday that it took lawmen 34 minutes to respond to an emergency call from a neighbour at 5:49 p.m. EST (2249 GMT) on the night of the crime.

"It wouldn't have mattered to the outcome if we had had a deputy a block away," Henderson told reporters, adding that the victim was stabbed six times in the chest, including one wound to the heart. "The call came in a shift-change time; we were having a busy day (and) there was rush-hour traffic. At the time we received that call there were no deputies available."
Henderson said investigators were trying to determine if Singleton might have any links to several unsolved murders of local prostitutes.
Although he was registered in Florida as a convicted felon, no attempt was made to keep track of his movements, said Lt. David Gee of the Hillsborough County Sheriff's office.
Singleton had no job and few friends in Tampa and supported himself on a small Merchant Marine pension and handouts from his family, according to local press reports.
Florida has a sexual predators notification law, under which neighbours of released convicts must be notified, but it went into effect in 1994 so did not apply to Singleton.
